data.narrative: The student decomposed the Team Collaboration request into 12 bounded tasks with dependencies, acceptance criteria, and three ready-to-run prompts. They reviewed the dependency chain, corrected an ordering issue, and investigated the supplied conflicting-assumption scenario without claiming that an unobserved implementation conflict occurred. The feature itself has not been implemented, so final quality reflects the planning artifact rather than a shipped product.

dimension_scores.observation: Produced a detailed task tree with scoped tasks, context, outputs, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and change budgets.
dimension_scores.evidence: Created 12 tasks (TC-01 to TC-12), each with a change budget of 150 lines or less, and included full prompts for TC-01, TC-02, and TC-03.

dimension_scores.observation: Audited dependencies and assumptions, then documented the actual handoff ambiguity and security prerequisites.
dimension_scores.evidence: Corrected the dependency-chain section and documented that TC-01 creates the User model, TC-02 consumes it, and team membership is introduced in TC-04.

dimension_scores.observation: Improved the task tree through a focused correction and a separate investigation rather than repeatedly rewriting the whole plan.
dimension_scores.evidence: Requested a corrected topological order and longest dependency chain, then added the BREAK investigation to the same task-tree document.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose progressive decomposition while identifying cross-cutting risks and refusing to treat an illustrative conflict as an actual finding.
dimension_scores.evidence: Recorded that the supplied owner_id/team_members mismatch did not apply and identified the identity-provider contract as a prerequisite before authentication implementation.

dimension_scores.observation: Produced a substantial planning artifact, but the Team Collaboration feature has not been implemented or verified end-to-end.
dimension_scores.evidence: The task tree and its verification command are present, but no Team Collaboration application code or feature tests were added.

strengths: Decomposed a broad feature request into 12 bounded tasks with explicit inputs, outputs, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
Identified identity verification, invitation delivery, authorization, and replay risks before implementation.
Used evidence to correct the dependency plan and distinguish the supplied hypothetical conflict from the actual task handoff.
growth_areas: Before implementation, resolve the trusted identity-provider and invitation-delivery decisions, then execute TC-01 and verify its model and migration before using its outputs in TC-02.
data.recommendation: Resolve the identity-provider contract and product-scope prerequisites, then implement only TC-01 in a separate branch and verify its migration and tests before proceeding to TC-02.

public_evidence.student_action: Directed an AI agent to create and revise a 12-task implementation plan, then independently checked the task list and documented the dependency investigation.
public_evidence.technical_detail: progress/ai-augmented-engineering/module-02/task-tree.md; tasks TC-01 through TC-12; dependency chain and BREAK investigation.
public_evidence.proof: File verification showed task-tree.md exists at 37 KB; grep output displayed TC-01 through TC-12, the three task prompts, the eight-task longest dependency chain, and the BREAK investigation.
public_evidence.ability: Prompt decomposition, dependency analysis, and evidence-based review of AI-generated plans.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the ability to turn a broad feature request into bounded, reviewable engineering work while identifying integration and security prerequisites.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Selected a progressive approach and planned to use verified outputs from earlier tasks to refine later tasks.
Documented task inputs, outputs, dependencies, and corrected the longest dependency chain.
Investigated the supplied conflict and documented why it did not apply to TC-01 and TC-02.

teaching_approaches.detail: Used the team-invitation feature to break a broad requirement into smaller tasks with explicit acceptance criteria.

learning_style_signals: Benefits from step-by-step instructions with one command and output review at a time.
